newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberian peacekeepers designate disarmament points.
newsitem.headline: Liberian peacekeepers designate disarmament points.

text.p: The West African peacekeeping force in Liberia, ECOMOG, on Thursday designated 11 locations for the disarming of Liberia's warring militias due to begin on Friday.

The three most powerful guerrilla armies are each assigned a disarmament centre in their strongholds, force commander General Victor Malu said in detailing the key part of the process to end nearly seven years of civil war.
One is the Barclay Training Centre barracks bastion of the ULIMO-J Krahn militia which was at the centre of ethnic warfare that devastated the capital in April and May.
Kakata, north of Monrovia, will be the assembly point for guerrillas of chief warlord Charles Taylor whose National Patriotic Front of Liberia launched civil war in December 1989.
Disarmament of the ULIMO-K faction of Alhaji Kromah will centre around a location in his northwestern stronghold town of Voinjama.
Other locations include the ports of Grenville and Buchanan and the western town of Tubmanburg where ECOMOG and Krahn guerrillas clashed last December and January.
Malu told reporters ECOMOG was prepared to use force against any warlord blocking the disarmament of an estimated 60,000 guerrillas, which is a prelude to elections set for next May.

"I have made clear my objection to anyone putting any impediment in the way of a smooth and successful implementation of this phase of the peace process," said the Nigerian general, whose country leads the ECOMOG force.
Peacekeepers have been deploying across the country since Tuesday.

The disarmament, due to be completed by the end of January, is part of a peace timetable brokered by West African leaders in August after a dozen earlier deals collapsed. West African leaders threatened sanctions against any warlord derailing the process.
Freed American slaves established Liberia in 1847. The war has killed well over 150,000 people.
